contents.title: Introduction to NestJS and Building Production-Ready Backends
contents.description: This reading introduces NestJS, explains why it is widely used in modern backend systems, and shows how it helps developers build scalable and maintainable applications.
contents.body:
## What is NestJS?

NestJS is a backend framework built on top of Node.js. It uses TypeScript by default and is heavily inspired by Angular architecture.

NestJS helps developers build applications that are:

- Structured
- Scalable
- Maintainable

---

## Core Architecture

NestJS follows a **module-based architecture**, where everything is organized into modules.

A typical module includes:

- Controllers (handle requests)
- Services (business logic)
- Providers (dependency injection)

Example:

```ts
@Module({
  controllers: [UserController],
  providers: [UserService],
})
export class UserModule {}
```

---

## Dependency Injection (DI)

NestJS uses DI to manage dependencies between classes.

```ts
@Injectable()
export class UserService {
  findAll() {
    return []
  }
}
```

Inject into controller:

```ts
constructor(private readonly userService: UserService) {}
```

👉 Benefits:

- Loose coupling
- Easier testing
- Cleaner architecture

---

## Request Lifecycle

The request lifecycle in NestJS:

1. Middleware
2. Guards
3. Interceptors (before)
4. Pipes
5. Controller
6. Interceptors (after)
7. Exception Filters

👉 This makes NestJS highly suitable for production systems.

---

## Building REST APIs

NestJS provides full REST support:

```ts
@Controller("users")
export class UserController {
  @Get()
  findAll() {}

  @Post()
  create() {}

  @Put(":id")
  update() {}

  @Delete(":id")
  remove() {}
}
```

---

## Why Use NestJS?

- Clear architecture (enterprise-ready)
- TypeScript-first approach
- Built-in best practices
- Easy to scale into microservices

If you want to build real-world systems (not just CRUD demos), NestJS is a strong choice.

translations.value: Giới thiệu NestJS và cách xây dựng Backend chuẩn production
Bài đọc này giúp bạn hiểu NestJS là gì, tại sao nó được sử dụng rộng rãi trong các hệ thống backend hiện đại, và cách nó giúp bạn xây dựng ứng dụng theo hướng scalable và maintainable.

## NestJS là gì?

NestJS là một framework backend được xây dựng trên Node.js, sử dụng TypeScript làm ngôn ngữ chính và lấy cảm hứng từ kiến trúc của Angular.

NestJS giúp bạn xây dựng ứng dụng theo hướng:

- Có cấu trúc rõ ràng
- Dễ mở rộng (scalable)
- Dễ bảo trì (maintainable)

---

## Kiến trúc cốt lõi

NestJS sử dụng mô hình **module-based architecture**, nghĩa là mọi thứ được tổ chức theo module.

Một module thường bao gồm:

- Controller (xử lý request)
- Service (xử lý logic)
- Provider (dependency injection)

Ví dụ:

```ts
@Module({
  controllers: [UserController],
  providers: [UserService],
})
export class UserModule {}
```

---

## Dependency Injection (DI)

NestJS sử dụng DI để quản lý dependency giữa các class.

```ts
@Injectable()
export class UserService {
  findAll() {
    return []
  }
}
```

Controller có thể inject service:

```ts
constructor(private readonly userService: UserService) {}
```

👉 Giúp code:

- Tách biệt logic
- Test dễ hơn
- Không bị tightly coupled

---

## Request Lifecycle

Flow xử lý request trong NestJS:

1. Middleware
2. Guards
3. Interceptors (before)
4. Pipes
5. Controller
6. Interceptors (after)
7. Exception Filters

👉 Đây là lý do NestJS rất phù hợp cho production system.

---

## Xây dựng REST API

NestJS hỗ trợ đầy đủ REST:

```ts
@Controller("users")
export class UserController {
  @Get()
  findAll() {}

  @Post()
  create() {}

  @Put(":id")
  update() {}

  @Delete(":id")
  remove() {}
}
```

---

## Tại sao nên dùng NestJS?

- Kiến trúc rõ ràng (enterprise-ready)
- TypeScript first
- Built-in best practices
- Dễ scale sang microservices

👉 Nếu bạn muốn build system thật (không phải demo CRUD), NestJS là lựa chọn rất tốt.

```ts
  controllers: [UserController],
  providers: [UserService],
})
export class UserModule {}
```

---

## Dependency Injection (DI)

NestJS uses DI to manage dependencies between classes.

```ts
@Injectable()
export class UserService {
  findAll() {
    return []
  }
}
```

Inject into controller:

```ts
constructor(private readonly userService: UserService) {}
```

👉 Benefits:

- Loose coupling
- Easier testing
- Cleaner architecture

---

## Request Lifecycle

The request lifecycle in NestJS:

1. Middleware
2. Guards
3. Interceptors (before)
4. Pipes
5. Controller
6. Interceptors (after)
7. Exception Filters

👉 This makes NestJS highly suitable for production systems.

---

## Building REST APIs

NestJS provides full REST support:

```ts
@Controller("users")
export class UserController {
  @Get()
  findAll() {}

  @Post()
  create() {}

  @Put(":id")
  update() {}

  @Delete(":id")
  remove() {}
}
```

---

## Why Use NestJS?

- Clear architecture (enterprise-ready)
- TypeScript-first approach
- Built-in best practices
- Easy to scale into microservices

If you want to build real-world systems (not just CRUD demos), NestJS is a strong choice.

contents.title: API Gateway Pattern
contents.description: A single entry point for clients to route requests and handle basic authentication before reaching downstream services.
contents.body:
## What is an API Gateway?
In a multi-service system, if clients call each service directly:
- Clients must know many different endpoints
- Authentication/rate-limiting/logging becomes inconsistent
- Internal changes can easily break client contracts

An API Gateway sits in front of services as an **entry point**:
- Routing requests to the right service
- Basic auth (validate tokens, attach user context)
- Rate limiting, logging, request/response transformation (as needed)

## When to use it
- Many services and many client types
- Need standardized auth/rate limit/observability
- Want to decouple public API contracts from internal topology

## Pitfalls
- The gateway can become a choke point if not scaled properly
- Avoid putting heavy business logic into the gateway

translations.value: API Gateway Pattern
Một "cổng vào" duy nhất cho client để routing request và thực hiện các bước auth cơ bản trước khi đi vào các service phía sau.

## API Gateway là gì?
Trong hệ thống nhiều service, nếu client gọi trực tiếp từng service thì:
- Client phải biết nhiều endpoint khác nhau
- Khó đồng bộ auth/ratelimit/logging
- Thay đổi nội bộ làm vỡ contract với client

API Gateway giải quyết bằng cách đứng trước các service như một **entry point**:
- Routing (định tuyến) request đến đúng service
- Auth cơ bản (validate token, attach user context)
- Rate limiting, logging, request/response transformation (tuỳ nhu cầu)

## Khi nào dùng?
- Nhiều service, nhiều client
- Cần chuẩn hoá auth/rate limit/observability
- Muốn tách "public API contract" khỏi internal service topology

## Pitfalls
- Gateway có thể thành "choke point" nếu không scale tốt
- Đừng nhồi quá nhiều business logic vào gateway

contents.title: Backend for Frontend (BFF)
contents.description: Split backend layers per client type (web/mobile) to optimize API contracts, reduce coupling, and avoid a "one size fits all" backend.
contents.body:
## What is BFF?
BFF (Backend for Frontend) means having a dedicated backend layer for each client:
- `web-bff` for web
- `mobile-bff` for mobile

It helps optimize:
- Data shape for UI needs (less over/under-fetching)
- Latency and number of round trips
- Versioning and rollout per client

## When to use it
- Multiple clients with different data needs (web vs mobile)
- Need an aggregation layer that composes data from many services
- Want to decouple release cycles between clients

## Pitfalls
- Logic duplication across BFFs without shared patterns/libraries
- BFF should not own core domain business rules (keep them in services)

contents.description: Compare synchronous service-to-service communication using REST and gRPC, and learn how to choose based on latency, contracts, and ecosystem constraints.
contents.body:
## REST (HTTP/JSON)
Pros:
- Easy to debug and integrate (curl, browser, logs)
- Great for public APIs with broad tooling support

Cons:
- Heavier payloads (JSON) and parsing overhead
- Contracts can be "loose" without OpenAPI/validation

## gRPC (HTTP/2 + Protobuf)
Pros:
- Fast and compact (binary), great for internal calls
- Strong contracts (proto), codegen, and streaming support

Cons:
- Harder to debug (binary payloads)
- Not browser-native like REST

## Quick decision guide
- Public API / widest compatibility: REST
- High-volume internal calls + strict contracts: gRPC
- Need streaming for internal flows: gRPC streaming

contents.title: Event-Driven Architecture (Kafka)
contents.description: Use Kafka (or a similar broker) to enable asynchronous communication between services, reduce coupling, and scale workflows reliably.
contents.body:
## What is event-driven?
Instead of service A calling service B synchronously, A **publishes an event** (e.g. `OrderCreated`) and consumers (other services) process it independently.

Benefits:
- Less coupling (A does not need to know B)
- Higher throughput (async processing, batching/streaming)
- Easy to add new consumers without changing producers

## When to use Kafka
- High event volume, need durability and replay
- Need ordering per key via partitions
- Large systems where workflows are split into async steps

## Common pitfalls
- Idempotency is mandatory (handle duplicates safely)
- Retries and DLQ to avoid stuck messages
- Observability: consumer lag and consumer health

translations.value: Event-Driven Architecture (Kafka)
Dùng Kafka (hoặc message broker tương tự) để xử lý bất đồng bộ giữa các service, giảm coupling và tăng khả năng scale cho các workflow.

## Event-Driven là gì?
Thay vì service A gọi sync sang service B, A **publish event** (vd: `OrderCreated`) và các consumer (service khác) xử lý độc lập.

Lợi ích:
- Giảm coupling (A không cần biết B)
- Tăng throughput (async, xử lý theo batch/stream)
- Dễ mở rộng thêm consumer mới mà không sửa producer

## Khi nào dùng Kafka?
- Nhiều sự kiện, cần durability + replay
- Cần xử lý stream theo partition (ordering theo key)
- Hệ thống lớn cần tách workflow thành các bước async

## Pitfalls cần nhớ
- Idempotency (xử lý lặp) là bắt buộc
- Retry/DLQ để tránh message kẹt
- Observability (lag, consumer health)

## How Pub/Sub works
- A producer publishes events to a topic
- Multiple consumer groups subscribe to the same topic
- Each group can process the event differently (e.g. send email, update search index, create invoices)

## When to use it
- One event should trigger multiple independent actions
- You want to add features by adding consumers (without changing producers)

## Production checklist
- Stable event schemas (versioning)
- Idempotent consumers
- Retry + DLQ
- Monitor consumer lag

contents.title: Choosing communication styles between services
contents.description: Choose the right communication approach (sync/async) based on latency needs, consistency requirements, and operational complexity.
contents.body:
## Questions to decide quickly
1) **Do you need the result immediately?**
- Yes → sync (REST/gRPC)
- No → async (Kafka/queue)

2) **Do you require strong end-to-end consistency?**
- Yes → consider sync boundaries and clear transaction ownership
- No → async + eventual consistency (saga/outbox)

3) **Is throughput/fanout large?**
- Large fanout → async is often a better fit

## Practical principles
- Prefer simplicity: use sync if it is sufficient
- Add async only with a clear reason (scale, decoupling, fanout)
- With async, always design idempotency and retries

1) **Có cần kết quả ngay không?**
- Có → sync (REST/gRPC)
- Không → async (Kafka/queue)

2) **Có cần strong consistency end-to-end không?**
- Có → cân nhắc sync + transaction boundary rõ ràng

## Nguyên tắc thực tế
- Ưu tiên đơn giản: sync nếu đủ
- Chỉ thêm async khi có lý do rõ ràng (scale, decouple, fanout)
- Luôn thiết kế idempotency và retry khi dùng async

contents.title: Sync vs Async: when to use which?
contents.description: Understand when to use sync calls (REST/gRPC) versus async messaging (Kafka) to optimize UX, reliability, and scalability.
contents.body:
## Sync (REST/gRPC)
Good when:
- You need an immediate user-facing response (login, checkout step, validation)
- The workflow is short with few dependencies

Risks:
- Cascading failures when downstream is slow/unavailable
- Latency adds up across chained calls

## Async (Kafka/queue)
Good when:
- Background processing (emails, reports, indexing)
- Large fanout across many consumers
- High throughput with built-in retry semantics

Risks:
- Eventual consistency (delayed visibility)
- Requires idempotency + retry/DLQ discipline

## Rule of thumb
- "Need now" user actions → sync
- Background/scale/fanout → async
- Common hybrid: sync accept request + async handle post-processing

Hiểu khi nào nên dùng sync (REST/gRPC) và khi nào nên dùng async (Kafka) để tối ưu trải nghiệm, độ tin cậy và khả năng mở rộng.

## Sync (REST/gRPC)
Phù hợp khi:
- Cần phản hồi ngay cho user (login, checkout step, validate input)
- Workflow ngắn, ít phụ thuộc

Rủi ro:
- Cascade failure nếu downstream chậm/timeout
- Latency cộng dồn theo chuỗi call

## Async (Kafka/queue)
Phù hợp khi:
- Xử lý nền (send email, generate report, indexing)
- Fanout nhiều consumer
- Cần throughput cao, retry tự nhiên

Rủi ro:
- Eventual consistency (trễ hiển thị)
- Cần idempotency + retry/DLQ

## Rule of thumb
- User-facing "need now" → sync
- Background/scale/fanout → async
- Có thể mix: sync nhận request + async xử lý hậu kỳ
